fixes.find: Short cycling is a control or a safety-trip problem. Adding refrigerant to a system that cycles every few minutes usually hides the real fault.
fixes.replace: Short cycling can come from controls, a safety trip or oversized capacity, and only measured checks separate them. Adding refrigerant without those checks can hide the real fault.
fixes.why: MAJOR #3: timing/category-as-diagnosis softened

fixes.find: Ice on the coil or the copper line means the system should be switched to fan only before anyone arrives. Running a compressor through ice is how a repair becomes a replacement.
fixes.replace: Ice on the coil or the copper line means cooling should be turned off. Fan-only thawing suits only dry, safe equipment where the manual allows it; running a compressor through ice can turn a repair into a replacement.
fixes.why: MAJOR #2: fan-only made conditional on dry, safe equipment

fixes.find: Look for a tripped breaker and reset it once only
fixes.replace: Leave a tripped breaker off and arrange diagnosis rather than resetting it. For a burning smell or smoke, leave the building and call 911 from outside
fixes.why: CRITICAL #1: unqualified breaker reset instruction removed

fixes.find: Set the system to fan only and change the air filter
fixes.replace: Turn cooling off and let the ice melt; run the fan alone only if the equipment is dry, no water is near wiring and the manual allows it
fixes.why: MAJOR #2: fan-only made conditional

fixes.find: Cycle length is the first clue, because timing the on-cycles and the off-cycles narrows the cause. Pressures read through a full cycle show whether a high-pressure or low-pressure switch is tripping. Refrigerant added without that data usually hides the fault for a week.
fixes.replace: Cycle timing is worth noting, but timing alone does not identify the fault. Pressures read through a full cycle, with control and wiring checks, show whether a pressure switch is tripping or a control is dropping out. Refrigerant added without that data can hide the fault.
fixes.why: MAJOR #3: timing-as-diagnosis replaced with measured checks

fixes.find: City & Suburban diagnoses the cause before anything is quoted, and on this symptom the timing comes first. Two to five minutes with cold air at the register points at controls. A cycle that ends with the outdoor unit stopping, while the indoor fan runs on, points at a protection trip. Coil, filter and the wiring at both ends all belong in the same diagnostic, because each one can raise pressure.
fixes.replace: City & Suburban diagnoses the cause before anything is quoted. Short cycles with cold air at the register can come from a control fault, but measured checks have to confirm it. A cycle that ends with the outdoor unit stopping, while the indoor fan runs on, can indicate a protection trip. Coil condition, the filter and the wiring at both ends all belong in the same diagnostic.
fixes.why: MAJOR #3: timing-as-diagnosis and 'each raises pressure' assertion removed

fixes.find: On-cycles of two to five minutes with cold air still at the register: thermostat location and wiring come first.
fixes.replace: On-cycles of a few minutes with cold air still at the register: thermostat location and wiring are possible causes to check, not a confirmed diagnosis.
fixes.why: MAJOR #3: timing-as-diagnosis softened

fixes.find: a pressure switch or an overload is tripping.
fixes.replace: a pressure switch or an overload may be tripping.
fixes.why: MAJOR #3: deterministic diagnosis softened

fixes.find: The first step is fan only, so the coil can thaw, because readings taken on ice mean nothing.
fixes.replace: The first step is to stop cooling so the coil can thaw, because readings taken on ice mean nothing. Running the fan alone helps only when the equipment is dry and the manual allows it; with overflow or water near wiring, switch the system off and keep away.
fixes.why: MAJOR #2: fan-only made conditional; shutdown for water near wiring

fixes.find: City & Suburban diagnoses the cause before anything is quoted, and on a frozen coil that means working from a clear coil. Airflow across the evaporator coil is measured first, with filter and blower condition. Charge, superheat and subcooling are read once the coil is clear and dry.
fixes.replace: City & Suburban diagnoses the cause before anything is quoted, and on a frozen coil a sound diagnosis works from a clear coil. Airflow across the evaporator coil should be checked first, with filter and blower condition. Charge, superheat and subcooling mean something only once the coil is clear and dry.
fixes.why: Unregistered procedure recast as good practice

fixes.find: That decision is better made with numbers than at the end of a hot week.
fixes.replace: Finding that leak is better done with numbers than at the end of a hot week.

fixes.find: never got up sold.” City & Suburban prices upfront, with no hidden fees.
fixes.replace: never got up sold.” That is one customer's account of pricing, not evidence of how a leak was found; repeat recharges are still a reason to ask for a leak search. City & Suburban prices upfront, with no hidden fees.
fixes.why: MAJOR #4: review kept as customer report only

fixes.find: A frozen coil needs several hours on fan only to thaw completely. Setting the system to fan and changing the filter before the appointment leaves a clear, dry coil. Airflow and charge readings only mean something in that state.
fixes.replace: A frozen coil can take several hours to thaw completely. Turn cooling off and let it melt; run the fan alone only if the equipment is dry, no water is near wiring and the manual allows it. Airflow and charge readings only mean something once the coil is clear and dry.
fixes.why: MAJOR #2: fan-only pro tip made conditional

fixes.replace: Water around an air conditioner is usually condensate that failed to drain.

fixes.replace: Seasonal drain and pan checks are maintenance work; ask whether a cooling maintenance plan includes them. Plan members get priority dispatch.

fixes.replace: Chicago's code sets a minimum temperature for heat.

fixes.find: Nothing comparable covers cooling, so a July failure is settled by scheduling rather than by ordinance.
fixes.replace: Cooling rules are narrower: Chicago code 14X-8-803.4 requires cooling for common gathering spaces in certain large or high-rise residential buildings, not for every dwelling unit, so confirm current requirements with the City.
fixes.why: CRITICAL: false blanket ordinance statement replaced with narrow 14X-8-803.4 distinction

fixes.find: A breaker that trips once may be heat or a sagging supply; a breaker that trips twice is reporting a fault.
fixes.replace: A single trip can come from heat or a sagging supply, but the cause still needs diagnosis before the circuit is used again.
fixes.why: CRITICAL #1: implied reset-once instruction removed

fixes.find: Reset once only. A second trip means the system stays off until the electrical side is tested.
fixes.replace: Leave the circuit off and do not reset it. The system stays off until the electrical side is tested.
fixes.why: CRITICAL #1: unqualified reset instruction removed

fixes.find: Switch it off at the disconnect and book a diagnostic the same day.
fixes.replace: For a burning smell or smoke, leave the building and call 911 from outside without approaching the unit. For noise or heat alone, turn cooling off at the thermostat and book a diagnostic.
fixes.why: Safety: burning odor means leave and call 911, not approach the disconnect
